text:
Connor McDavid's point streak ended at 23 games on Thursday, a 3-1 loss in Tampa, as Oilersnation noted. It was a rare off night for a team second in the league at 17-4-3, one point behind Minnesota, and for a coach, Mike Babcock, who has spent the week explaining why he split McDavid and Leon Draisaitl.

Here is the part the record hides. Edmonton gets almost exactly half of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 50.2%, and only 47% at five on five. The Oilers have 37 points against about 27 our numbers think the play earned, and they've scored 22.7 more goals than their chances. Some is elite finishing, some a hot net: Tristan Jarry is at .951 over his last five starts, and Devon Levi, picked up from Buffalo, has 10 wins in 11 games, a club record per one report.

The good stuff is very good. McDavid, Draisaitl and Vasily Podkolzin together have outscored teams 22-6 with 62% of the chances, and Evan Bouchard, named the early Norris favourite in NHL.com's Trophy Tracker, has 14 points in his last 10. The worry is depth: the Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line has 31% of the chances and has been outscored 11-5, and the Connor Murphy and Ryan Shea pair sits at 43%.

The Oilers are 98% to make the playoffs by our odds. What we'd watch is whether the split stars can tilt the ice before the goaltending cools.
headline: The Oilers are winning on goaltending and stars
